Ideo. or det. in rthty 'baker'. Hence det. in the related words [t]rtḥ[/t] 'restrain'; [t]itḥ[/t] 'prison'. Probably for some reason connected with its use ideo. or det. in [t]ḫn[/t](r)i 'restrain'; [t]ḫnrtm[/t] var, [t]ḫnt[/t], 'harem'. Through similarity in hieratic sometimes substituted for D 19 or D 20, ex. ssnt 'breath'.

[t]tḥnt[/t] 'fayence'; [t]ḥts[/t] 'inaugurate (a feast)'. In group-writing or or is phon. t, ex. Ti, name of a Syrian locality.

sign list.description: club used by fullers in washing

For see D 31.
Det. in [t]ḫꜥq[/t] 'shave'.
Ideo. or det. in [t]mḫꜢt[/t] 'balance'.
Det. in [t]wṯst[/t] 'post (of balance)' and in the related verb [t]wṯs[/t] 'lift', 'carry', 'wear'. Secondarily also det. in [t]ṯsi[/t] (ṯśi) 'raise', 'lift'.
Use as last, ex. [t]wṯsw[/t] 'those who have worn'. Also, owing to similarity in hieratic, used for T 13, ex. rs-tp 'vigilant'.

sign list.description: plummet used in connection with the balance
sign list.notes: Det. in [t]tḫ[/t] 'plummet'.

Det. rope, exx. [t]nwḥ[/t] 'rope'; [t]hꜢtt[/t] 'front-rope' of ship; actions with rope or cord, exx. [t]itḥ[/t] 'drag'; [t]ṯs[/t] 'tie'; [t]mnḫ[/t] 'string' beads; [t]šni[/t] 'encircle', 'surround'. Probably from [t]šnw[/t] 'network', phon. or phon. det. [t]šn[/t] in [t]šnt[/t] 'dispute', the relations of which with [t]šni[/t] 'exorcise', 'litigate' and with [t]šnṯ[/t] 'contend' require further study. Another possibly related word is [t]št[/t] ([t]šnt[/t]?) 'hundred'. A similar, but doubtless different, sign is det. in [t]ḫꜢb[/t] 'bent appendage' (of metal?) belonging to the crown . For as substitute for G 43, see Z 7.

sign list.description: bolt O 34 combined with the cord V 1 used for drawing it
sign list.notes: Ideo. in [t]sṯꜢ[/t] (śṯꜢ), later [t]stꜢ[/t], 'drag', 'draw'; hence phon. [t]sṯꜢ[/t] in [t]sṯꜢt[/t] 'aroura'. For an unknown reason det. in [t]Ꜣs[/t] 'hasten'.

sign list.description: the same sign with three cords (Dyn. XVIII)
sign list.notes: Phon. [t]sṯꜢw[/t] in [t]R-sṯꜢw[/t] 'necropolis', particularly that of the Memphitic god Sokar.
Cf. [t]wꜢw[/t] 'lassoes'. hence phon. [t]wꜢ[/t], exx. [t]wꜢ[/t] 'far'; [t]wꜢḥ[/t] 'place', 'endure'.
Det. in [t]snṯ[/t] (śnṯ) 'plan', 'plot out', 'found'.

sign list.description: cord (in early exx. double and looped at top on left)
sign list.notes: Ideo. or semi-ideo. or det. in [t]šs[/t], var. O.K. šś, 'cord', 'rope'. Hence phon. [t]šs[/t] (šś), exx. [t]šs[/t] 'alabaster'; [t]išst[/t] 'what?'. There has been much confusion with 𓎤 [t]V[/t]33: (1) in the words 'linen', 'cloth', 'thing', 'concern' and 'corn', all originally reading śšr: however, the fact of the confusion, together with certain writings with metathesis [t]šsr[/t], make the usually accepted reading [t]šs[/t] still just defensible, for final r usually falls; (2) as det. in [t]ꜥrf[/t] 'tie up', 'pack'; (3) as phon. g in hieratic, where the two signs are not distinguished in early times; (4) as det. clothes, ex. isywt 'rags'; however, this employment to replace 𓋳 [t]S[/t]28 does not appear before Dyn. XIX.

sign list.description: loop of cord with the ends downward
sign list.notes: Cf. [t]šni[/t] 'encircle'. Hence phon. [t]šn[/t]. exx. [t]šn[/t] 'tree'; [t]šnꜥ[/t] 'repel'.
Use as last.
Det. in [t]šnw[/t] 'cartouche'.
Det. in [t]šnw[/t] 'circuit'; rn 'name'; also in names of kings and other royal personages, in which case the component signs are written inside it.

sign list.description: sign probably later taken to be a cartouche cut in half and reversed.
sign list.notes: Det. in dni 'dam off', 'restrain'. The hieratic equivalent of the same sign serves also as det. in [t]pḫꜢ[/t] 'split'. It seems doubtful whether the hieratic word usually transcribed as dyt (dwyt?) 'shriek' was originally written with this sign.

Det. bind, exx. [t]sšd[/t] 'head-band'; [t]ꜥnḫ[/t] 'garland'; [t]fḫ[/t] 'loose', whence [t]fḫ[/t] 'depart'; from the last, phon. det. in [t]tꜢw[/t] [t]Fnḫw[/t] 'Phoenician lands'. det. papyrus-books, exx. [t]šfdw[/t] 'papyrus'; snn 'deed'. Phon. or phon. det. [t]ꜥrq[/t] (from [t]ꜥrq[/t] 'bind on') in [t]ꜥrq[/t] 'swear'; [t]ꜥrqy[/t] 'last day' of the month.
Cf. Pyr. [t]ṯṯt[/t] 'fetterer (?)'. Phon. [t]ṯ[/t]. Sometimes also, by a false archaism, for t.

sign list.description: the last, with an added diacritical tick
sign list.notes: Phon. [t]ṯ[/t], both in hieroglyphic and hieratic, but apparently only in a few words, doubtless words in which the value [t]ṯ[/t] had not changed into t, exx. [t]ṯsi[/t] 'lift'; Ṯṯi 'Tjeti', a man's name.
In [t]iṯi[/t], in M.E. often iti, 'seize'.

sign list.description: looped cord serving as hobble for cattle
sign list.notes: Ideo. in O.K. [t]sꜢ[/t] ([t]zꜢ[/t]) 'hobble'. Hence phon. [t]sꜢ[/t] ([t]zꜢ[/t]) in [t]sꜢ[/t] 'protection'.

sign list.description: rolled up herdsman's shelter of papyrus (Dyn. XVIII)
sign list.notes: Ideo. in [t]sꜢ[/t], var. Pyr. [t]zꜢ[/t], 'protection'.
Use as last.

Ideo. or det. in [t]mḏt[/t] 'stable', '(cattle)-stall'. For unknown reasons, det. in [t]tmꜢ[/t] (from [t]ṯmꜢ[/t] ?) 'mat', whence phon. or phon. det. [t]ṯmꜢ[/t] ([t]tmꜢ[/t]) in [t]ṯmꜢ[/t] 'cadaster (?)' or kind of land (?); in [t]ẖꜢr[/t] 'sack' as measure of capacity; and in other names of woven or wickerwork objects. By confusion with an older sign for a palanquin or portable shrine, det. in qni 'palanquin', whence also in qni 'sheaf'; so too in [t]kꜢr[/t] 'shrine'; possibly also in [t]šṯyt[/t], name of the sanctuary of Sokar in Memphis. To be distinguished carefully from Aa 19.

sign list.description: the same without the cross-bar (cf. V 21)
sign list.notes: Cf. Syn. XIX [t]mḏwt[/t] 'stables'. Hence phon. [t]mḏ[/t] in [t]mḏw[/t] '10'.

sign list.description: combination of V 20 and I 10 (Dyn. XII onward)
sign list.notes:
Ideo. in [t]mḏt[/t] 'stable', 'cattle-stall'. Hence phon. [t]mḏ[/t] in [t]mḏ[/t] 'be deep' and derivatives.
For see M 28.
For unknown reason, phon. [t]mḥ[/t], exx. [t]mḥ[/t] 'fill'; [t]mḥnyt[/t] 'the coiled one', name of a snake.
Use as last.

sign list.description: cord wound on a stick (O.K. and M.K. form)
sign list.notes: For unkown reason, phon. [t]wḏ[/t] (later wd), exx. [t]wḏ[/t] 'command'; [t]wḏḥ[/t] (for [t]wdḥ[/t]) 'table of offerings'; [t]wḏb[/t] 'turn'.
Use as last.

Ideo. in [t]ꜥḏ[/t], also [t]ꜥd[/t], 'spool', 'reel'. Hence phon. or phon. det. [t]ꜥḏ[/t], later [t]ꜥd[/t], ex. [t]ꜥḏ[/t], var. [t]ꜥd[/t], 'be in good condition'; also [t]ꜥnḏ[/t] or [t]ꜥnd[/t], proved only in the case of [t]mꜥndt[/t], var. Pyr. [t]mꜥnḏt[/t], 'the morning-bark' of the sun-god.
Use as last.
Cf. with a smilar sign, [t]ḥꜥt[/t] 'wick'; hence phon. [t]ḥ[/t]. As late det. once in [t]tkꜢ[/t] 'candle'.

sign list.description: swab made from a hank of fibre (down to Dyn. XVIII identical for all uses)
sign list.notes: Det. in O.K. śk 'wipe'; hence phon. sk (śk), ex. ski 'perish'. For unknown reason, phon. or phon. det. [t]wꜢḥ[/t], ex. [t]wꜢḥ[/t] 'place', 'endure'. Also det. in [t]ḫsr[/t], var. Pyr. ḫśr, 'ward-off'. As corruption of a sign resembling M1, det. in [t]mꜥr[/t] 'fortunate'.

Ideo. in nbt 'basket'. Hence phon. in a few words reading nb, exx. nb 'lord'; nb 'every', 'all'.
For see O 9.
For unknown reason, phon. k.

sign list.description: the last, but with handle on opposite side
sign list.notes: Regularly in hieratic except in rare O.K. examples.

sign list.description: wickerwork frail (possibly also used as a float by hippopotamus-hunters)
sign list.notes: Det. in msnw, var. Dyn. mśn, 'harpooner'; hence (?) phon. msn (mśn) in Msn, a Lower Egyptian town near Qantarah. Possibly, but not certainly, the same sign in [t]gꜢwt[/t] 'bundles', 'tribute'; hence phon. det. [t]gꜢw[/t] in [t]gꜢw[/t] 'be narrow', and related words.

Ideo. or det. in [t]sšr[/t], var. O.K. śšr, var. Dyn. XVIII [t]šsr[/t], 'linen', 'cloth', cf. especially the compound [t]sšr[/t]-nsw, var. O.K. śšr-nzw, 'royal-linen', 'byssus'; the var. with V 6 makes the hitherto accepted reading [t]šs[/t]-nsw possible for Dyn. XVIII, as final r frequently fell away. Hence phon. [t]sšr[/t] in [t]sšr[/t], var. O.K. śšr, 'thing', 'concern'; also in [t]sšr[/t] 'corn'. Perhaps through connection with the stem found in [t]gꜢwt[/t] 'bundles' (see of V 32) or else with ggt 'kidney (?)' phon. g in a few words, exx. wgg 'misery'; Gbtyw 'Coptus', a town in Upper Egypt. Det. tie up, in [t]ꜥrf[/t] 'tie up', 'pack', 'envelop'; also perfume, because kept in bags of linen, ex. sty 'perfume', cf. R 9. As det. clothes not before Dyn. XIX, and then mainly in the form V 6 (see on that sign). Note that in M.K. hieratic is indistinguishable from V 6; in hieroglyphic the two are very often confused.
Use as last.
Use as last.
Det. in [t]ḥn[/t] ([t]ḥnt[/t] ?), name of a receptacle given to a temple. Hence (?) phon. or phon. det. [t]ḥn[/t], exx. [t]ḥnt[/t] 'occupations'; [t]ḥnty[/t] 'period', 'end'.
Det. in idr 'bandage', 'bind'. Phon. or phon. det. idr in idr 'herd'; note reading [t]kꜢ[/t] n idr 'bull of herd'. For the confusion of and N 41 see AEO. ii. 258.
Det. in wt 'bandage', 'mummy-cloth'. Later replaced by Aa 2.

sign list.category_group: W, Vessels of stone and earthenware
sign list.notes: Det. oil, unguent, exx. [t]mrḥt[/t] 'unguent'; [t]mḏt[/t] 'ointment'.

sign list.category_group: W, Vessels of stone and earthenware
sign list.description: sealed oil-jar, like W 1, but not showing tied ends
sign list.notes: Det. in [t]bꜢs[/t] (bꜢś) 'jar'. Phon. [t]bꜢs[/t] (bꜢś) in [t]BꜢstt[/t], var. O.K. BꜢśtt, '(the cat-goddess) Bastet'.

sign list.category_group: W, Vessels of stone and earthenware
sign list.description: basin of alabaster as used in purifications
sign list.notes: Det. in O.K. 𓈙𓋴𓍱𓎱 [t]š[/t]ś var. 𓍱𓎱 'alabaster'. Perhaps on account of the purifications characteristic of feasts, det. in 𓎛𓃀𓎳 var. Dyn. XVIII 𓎛𓃀𓎱 [t]ḥb[/t] 'feast'; hence semi-ideo. or phon. [t]ḥb[/t] in 𓎛𓎱𓃀𓀜 [t]ḥb[/t] 'mourn'. Abbrev. of 𓎛𓃀𓏏𓎱𓍼 [t]ḥbt[/t] 'ritual book' in 𓎴 [t]W[/t]5. Det. feast, exx. 𓇷𓅂𓎱 [t]psḏntyw[/t] 'New Moon festival'; 𓍯𓎼𓎱 [t]WꜢg[/t] 'Wag-festival'.

sign list.category_group: W, Vessels of stone and earthenware
sign list.notes: Ideo. or det. in [t]ḥb[/t] 'feast'. Det. feast (much rarer in M.E. than alone), ex. tp-rnpt 'feast of the first of the year'.

sign list.category_group: W, Vessels of stone and earthenware
sign list.notes: In [t]ẖry-ḥbt[/t] 'lector-priest', lit. 'he who is under (i.e. carries) the ritual book'.

sign list.category_group: W, Vessels of stone and earthenware
sign list.description: O.K. sign for a particular vessel
sign list.notes: In. [t]wḥt[/t] 'cauldron'. Later replaced by Aa 2.

sign list.category_group: W, Vessels of stone and earthenware
sign list.notes: Det. in [t]mꜢt[/t], var. O.K. [t]mꜢṯ[/t], 'red granite'; hence phon. det. [t]mꜢṯ[/t] in [t]mꜢṯ[/t] 'proclaim'. Det. in [t]Ꜣbw[/t] 'Elephantine', as source of the red granite; hence phon. det. [t]Ꜣb[/t] in [t]Ꜣbt[/t] 'family'.

sign list.category_group: W, Vessels of stone and earthenware
sign list.notes: In [t]Ꜣbw[/t] 'Elephantine' and [t]Ꜣbt[/t] 'family', see on W 7. The same sign may serve as the earlier form of [t]gꜢw[/t] 'V 32.

sign list.category_group: W, Vessels of stone and earthenware
sign list.notes: Det. in [t]nẖnm[/t], var. Pyr. [t]nšnm[/t], 'the [t]nẖnm[/t]-vase' with its specified oil. Hence (?) phon. [t]ẖnm[/t], exx. H̱nmw '(the ram-headed god) Khnum'; [t]ẖnm[/t] 'join'.

sign list.category_group: W, Vessels of stone and earthenware
sign list.description: cup (probably sometimes also a basket, cf. A 9)
sign list.notes: Det. in [t]iꜥb[/t], var. [t]ꜥꜥb[/t], 'cup'; hence phon. or phon. det. [t]iꜥb[/t], ex. [t]iꜥb[/t] 'unite'; [t]ꜥb[/t], ex. [t]m-ꜥb[/t] 'in the company of'. Det. in [t]wsḫ[/t] (wśḫ) 'cup'; hence phon. or phon. det. [t]wsḫ[/t] (wśḫ), exx. [t]wsḫ[/t] 'be wide'; [t]wsḫt[/t] 'hall'; [t]sḫw[/t] in [t]sḫw[/t] 'width'. Det. in [t]ḥnt[/t] 'cup'; hence phon. [t]ḥnt[/t] in [t]ḥnwt[/t] 'mistress'. Det. in [t]ꜥ[/t] 'cup'. In words reading [t]biꜢ[/t] sometimes replaces older N 41, ex. [t]biꜢw[/t] 'rare treasures'.

sign list.category_group: W, Vessels of stone and earthenware
sign list.description: pot perhaps used also as lamp (O.K.)
sign list.notes: Phon. [t]bꜢ[/t] in conjunction with G 29, ex. [t]bꜢ[/t] 'soul', or with E 10, ex. [t]BꜢ[/t]-pf(i) 'Bapfi', a god. Later superseded in these uses by R 7.

sign list.category_group: W, Vessels of stone and earthenware
sign list.description: (1) ring-stand for jars, (2) red earthenware pot (Dyn. XVIII form, round at bottom)
sign list.notes: (1) Ideo. or det. in nst 'seat'. For unknown reason, phon. g. (2) Ideo. or det. in [t]dšrt[/t] 'red pot'. (3) Occasionally substituted for O 45 in Dyn. XVIII, ex. ipt nsw 'king's harem'.

sign list.category_group: W, Vessels of stone and earthenware
sign list.notes: Use as last, in O.K. nśt 'seat' and as phon. g.

sign list.category_group: W, Vessels of stone and earthenware
sign list.description: red earthenware pot (O.K. form, round at bottom and plain)
sign list.notes: Use as W 11, in O.K. [t]dšrt[/t] 'red pot'. In M.K. a sign of this appearance is used for N 34.

sign list.category_group: W, Vessels of stone and earthenware
sign list.notes: Ideo. or det. in [t]ḥst[/t], var. O.K. [t]ḥzt[/t], 'water-pot'; hence phon. [t]ḥs[/t] ([t]ḥz[/t]), ex. [t]ḥsi[/t] 'praise'. Det. also in snb(t), var. Pyr. znbt, 'jar'.

sign list.category_group: W, Vessels of stone and earthenware
sign list.description: water-pot with water pouring from it
sign list.notes: Det. in qbb 'be cool' and derivatives; also in [t]qbḥ[/t] 'libate'.

sign list.category_group: W, Vessels of stone and earthenware
sign list.description: the same in a ring-stand W 12
sign list.notes: Ideo. or det. in [t]qbḥw[/t] 'libation' and the related words. Much more rarely det. in qbb 'be cool'.

sign list.category_group: W, Vessels of stone and earthenware
sign list.notes: Ideo. in [t]ḫntw[/t] 'racks for water-pots'. Hence phon. [t]ḫnt[/t], ex. [t]ḫnt[/t] 'in front of' and derivatives.

sign list.category_group: W, Vessels of stone and earthenware
sign list.notes: Use as last.

sign list.category_group: W, Vessels of stone and earthenware
sign list.description: milk-jug as carried in a net
sign list.notes: Det. in mhr 'milk-jug'. From a probably obsolete word mr 'milk-jug', phon. mi (old mr), exx. mi, var. Pyr. mr, 'like'; dmi 'town'; min 'today'.

sign list.category_group: W, Vessels of stone and earthenware
sign list.description: milk-jug with a leaf covering the milk
sign list.notes: Det. in irtt, var. O.K. [t]irṯt[/t], 'milk'.

sign list.category_group: W, Vessels of stone and earthenware
sign list.notes: Det. in irp 'wine'.

sign list.category_group: W, Vessels of stone and earthenware
sign list.notes: Ideo. or det. in [t]ḥnqt[/t] 'beer'. Det. pot, measure, exx. [t]qrḥt[/t] 'vessel'; ds (O.K. dś) 'des-measure'; offerings generally, in inw 'tribute'; notions connected with fluids, ex. [t]tḫi[/t] 'be drunken'. As det. in the group 'food and drink', see on X 2. Ideo. in wdpw 'butler'.

sign list.category_group: W, Vessels of stone and earthenware
sign list.notes: Use as last, but not specially in connection with beer. Exx. [t]qrḥt[/t] 'vessel'; [t]wrḥ[/t] 'anoint'. Also in wdpw 'butler', see on W 22.

sign list.category_group: W, Vessels of stone and earthenware
sign list.notes: Phon. nw, exx. nw (nyw) 'of', m. plur.; Nwt '(the goddess) Nut', probably so to be read (in spite of an obscure Pyr. var.) [t]ḥnw[/t] 'vessel'. For preferred writing of initial nw see on U 19; final nw is sometimes written , exx. mnw 'monument'; Ṯḥnw 'Libya'. Great difficulty is caused by 'primeval waters', which may have existed in two distince forms (1) niw or nww or nw, (2) nnw or nwnw. Phon. also in (cf. W 25) in ink 'I'. Phon. det. in [t]ḏꜢḏꜢt[/t] 'council'; whether the former writing has anything to do with [t]ḏꜢḏꜢw[/t] 'pot' is doubtful. So too from M.K. used in such words as qd 'build'; qd 'form'; the only phon. det. here is due to the stem meaning of qdi 'go round', while the later may be connected with qd 'fashion' pots. From M.K. onwards inexplically accompanies Aa 17, exx. [t]nḏ[/t] 'protect'; [t]nḏ[/t] 'ask'; and is found also in [t]Nḫbt[/t] '(the goddess) Nekhbet'. The writing for [t]m-ẖnw[/t] 'in', lit. 'in the interior (of)' has been explained as a rebus m(w) [t]ẖ[/t](r) nw 'water under pot'. Lastly, W24 occurs as occasional alternative to or as det. pot; hieratic often fails to distinguish these signs.

sign list.category_group: W, Vessels of stone and earthenware
sign list.notes: In ini 'bring', 'fetch'.
Use as last.

Ideo. (or semi-phon. t) in t 'bread'; (the accepted reading [t]tꜢ[/t] has no justification). Hence phon. t. Note the spellings for [t]it-nṯr[/t] 'god's father', name of a class of elder priests. In group-writing with and is used for t.
For see M 5.

Det. bread, exx. t 'bread'; [t]šns[/t] '[t]šns[/t]-loaf'. For t in group writing see on X 1. The groups or with , representing bread and beer with or without another sign for bread, occur as generic det. food, exx. [t]prt-ḫrw[/t] 'invocation offerings'; [t]šꜢb[/t] meal'; expanded still further in [t]ḥtp(w)-nṯr[/t] 'divine offerings'. On M.K. coffins sometimes replaces in Ḏḥwty 'Thoth' for superstitious reasons, and a similar or identical group serves also rarely for Gb '(the earth-god) Geb' or for I͗npw 'Anubis'. From the end of Dyn. XVIII is found as var. of [t]it-nṯr[/t] 'god's father', a priestly title, see above under X1.
Use as last. For as the earliest form of N 34 see on that sign.

Det. bread, food. exx. t 'bread'; [t]prt-ḫrw[/t] 'invocation offerings'; [t]snw[/t] 'food-offerings'. From this last, phon. det. sn (zn), exx. sni 'pass by'; Sni 'Senet', a fem. personal name; cf. also Pyr. iznii 'are opened'. In sni 'pass by' and snt 'likeness' X 4 is subsequently replaced by X 5, while Pyr. in zn 'open' later takes the form N 37, see on that sign. Also from [t]fqꜢ[/t] 'cake', phon. det. [t]fqꜢ[/t] in [t]fqꜢ[/t] 'reward'. As det. sometimes takes the place of W 3 (Dyns. XI. XII), ex. [t]ḥbw[/t] 'festivals'.
Det. bread, food (in hieratic only), exx. t 'bread'; [t]ꜥqw[/t] 'provisions'. From Dyn. XII usually takes the place of as phon. det. sn in hieroplyphic sni 'surpass'; m-snt-r 'in the likeness of'.

sign list.description: a round loaf bearing mark of the baker's fingers
sign list.notes: Det. in [t]pꜢt[/t] 'loaf'. Hence phon. det. in [t]pꜢt[/t] 'antiquity', 'primeval times' and the related words. Apt to be confused with N 9.

In. O.K. offerings-lists described as gśw 'half-loaves' or [t]pḏw[/t] '(pieces) spread out'. In Pyr. doubled is ideo. or det. food, exx. [t]wšb[/t] 'eat'; wnm 'eat'. After O.K. becomes indistinguishable from N 29 and is practically confined to the word wnm 'eat'. Exceptionally, however, as det. in snw 'food-offerings'.

sign list.description: conical loaf ? (in M.E. more often replaced by D 37)
sign list.notes: Ideo. give, in rdi 'give' and also in Pyr. for the more usual imperative imi 'give'. The use in both stems seems conclusively for the ideographic character of the sign. Possibly the earliest reading of the later stem rdi was [t]rḏi[/t], cf. the Pyr. var. for [t]rḏw[/t] 'efflux'; but verb forms with repetition of the sign doubtless indicate the reading dd; so in Pyr. already. From the same stem, phon. d (very rare), ex. dq(r) 'fruit'. The word 'provisions' probably reads di; in hieratic the inner markings are not shown, see before Z 9, and the word has, therefore, often been read śpd.

sign list.description: papyrus rolled up, tied, and sealed (from Dyn. XII on also vertically)
sign list.notes: Ideo. in [t]mḏꜢt[/t] 'papyrus-roll', 'book'. Hence phon. [t]mḏꜢt[/t] in [t]mḏꜢt[/t] '(sculptor's) chisel'. Det. writing and things written, exx. [t]sš[/t] 'write'; m(w)dt 'word'; [t]ḥqꜢ[/t] 'magic'; also abstract notions, exx. [t]mꜢꜥt[/t] 'truth'; [t]mꜢw[/t](y) 'be new'; [t]rḫ[/t] 'know'; [t]ꜥꜢ[/t] 'great'. In mathematical books and accounts is often abbrev. for dmd 'total'.

sign list.description: O.K. form of last (also vertically from Pyr. on in specific cases)
sign list.notes: Use as last.

sign list.description: scribe's outfit, consisting of palatte, bag for the powedered pigments, and reed holder
sign list.notes: Ideo. or det. in mnhd 'scribe's outfit'; also in [t]sšw[/t] 'writings' and the related words, cf. O.K. [t]zš[/t] 'write'. Perhaps because pigments were ground fine and smooth, det. in [t]nꜥꜥ[/t] 'smooth'; in the Ebers medical papyrus it is used as abbrev. for [t]snꜥꜥ[/t] 'made smooth', 'ground fine'. Also det. of the Pyr. word [t]ṯms[/t] 'red' with its later derivative tmsw 'injury', 'harm'.
Use as last.
For unknown reason, phon. mn, exx. mn 'remain'; I͗mn '(the god) Amun'; [t]mnḥ[/t] 'wax'.
Ideo. or det. in ib([t]Ꜣ[/t]) 'draughtsman'. Hence phon. [t]ibꜢ[/t] in [t]ibꜢ[/t](w), 'dances'.
Det. in bnt (bint) 'harp'.
Ideo. or det. in [t]sššt[/t] 'sistrum'. Between dyn. XIII-XVIII occasionally phon. [t]sḫm[/t] (because of [t]sḫm[/t], a kind of sistrum), ex. [t]sḫm[/t]-ir(y).f 'potentate'.

Ideo. or det. one, unity, exx. [t]wꜥ[/t] 'one', 7 'seven', lit. 'seven units'. Following an ideogram denotes that this means the actual thing that it depicts, exx. r 'mouth'; [t]ḏw[/t] 'mountain'; so too in duals and plurals, exx. [t]ꜥwy[/t] 'the two arms'; [t]sbꜢw[/t] 'stars'; [t]ḫꜢswt[/t] 'countries'; in fem. nouns the fem. ending t often intervenes, ex. [t]ḥst[/t] 'water-jar'. Such writings were often preceded in O.K. by phonetic signs; M.E. survivals of this practice are s 'man'; hrw 'day'. Ideo. with is occasionally followed by a det., ex. [t]Rꜥ[/t] 'Ra'. Misunderstanding of the function of often leads to its displacement, exx. with s 'man'; [t]š[/t] 'pool'. Also with with a later writing of [t]tꜢ[/t] 'earth'; dmi 'town' is likewise difficult to explain, as also are many later exx. of the stroke. Already in Pyr. cases occur of ideo. with being together transferred to a phonetic use; so often in M.E., exx. [t]ḥr[/t] 'upon'; [t]sꜢ[/t] 'son'; so particularly in group-writing, exx. r; [t]ṯ[/t]. Along similar lines with as det. towns. Occasionally in Dyn XII serves merely to fill empty space. In Pyr. was sometimes used (like diagonal stroke and ) to replace human figures, these being regarded as magically dangerous; so in M.K. coffins, exx. for i 'O'; extensions of this use appear to be the rare employment of as suffix 1st pers. sing. i 'I'; perhaps also the fairly common writing with replacing in s 'man.

sign list.description: stroke Z 1 thrice repeated (with various writings, vertical etc.)
sign list.notes:
Det. plurality, common from Dyn. IX onwards, following an ideo. or det. to show that it should be understood three times, exx. after for rnpwt 'years' for O.K. ; also with [t]nḏsw[/t] 'poor men'. Examples occur already in Pyr., but very rarely, ex. mrw 'canals'; these suggest as origin of the use a contraction of plurals like into plus , but since are found as plur. det. from Dyn. VI onward (exx. [t]wꜢwt[/t] 'roads', [t]nḏsw[/t] 'poor men') the use of as plur. det. cannot be dissociated entirely from the employment of , , or in Pyr. as substitute for signs representing human figures which were regarded as magically dangerous; see on Z 1; Z 5; N 33. In. M.E. Z 2 is found also with purely phonetic signs, exx. wrw 'great ones'; nfrw 'beautiful', m. plur.; nfrt 'beautiful', f. plur. Sometimes it marks plural meaning in words that are not themselves plural, exx. sn 'their'; [t]ẖnyt[/t] 'sailors', a fem. collective; [t]ꜥšꜢ[/t] 'many'; such plural meaning was probably felt by the Egyptians in words denoting foodstuffs, materials, etc., though singular in form, exx. t 'bread'; iwf 'flesh'; [t]ḥḏ[/t] 'silver'; so too in fem. participles with neuter meaning, exx. [t]ḏddt[/t] 'what was said', '(things) said'. Lastly, is found with abstracts ending in w, whether these are really plurals or not, exx. [t]šmsw[/t] 'following'; [t]nḏsw[/t] 'poverty'; soo too with fem. infinitives, if such they be, ex. mswt 'birth'. For the same sign vertically written in hieratic, see under Z 3 (occurs also as phon. det. in [t]ḫmt[/t] 'think').
For see on N33.

Use as last, common in hieroglyphic from Dyn. XII, rarer in hieratic.
For see on N 33.

sign list.description: two diagonal strokes (less often written straight)
sign list.notes: In Pyr. only as det. duality, exx. [t]ṯn[/t](i) 'you two' (cf. for the ending śni 'they two'); [t]ꜥw[/t](i), also [t]ꜥw[/t](y), 'the two arms'; and in O.K., ex. [t]pḥw[/t](i) 'end'. In some cases replaced human figures, these being deemed to be magically dangerous, exx. [t]Ꜣḫt[/t](i) 'the two glorious ones' for [t]sꜢt[/t](i) 'son and daughter'; t(w)twi 'the two images'. The last use survives in M.E. Šdty 'Crocodilopolite', where, however, the hieratic replaces, not dangerous singns, but signs difficult to draw; see below Z 5. Elsewhere in M.E. is always phon. y, through its constant association earlier with words of dual form, i.e. ending in i (y); exx. are .fy, var. Pyr. . fi, 'his two'; imnty 'western'; [t]sḏmty[/t].fy 'who will hear'. Except in compounds like the last y is always final consonant; it has its distinct uses, and is seldom interchangeable with it.

sign list.description: diagonal stroke as made in hieratic
sign list.notes: Identical in origin with stroke being used in Pyr. as substitute for human figures, these being considered magically dangerous, ex. śmśw 'elder' with replacing . In M.E. hieratic used only to replace dets. that were difficult to draw, exx. [t]Ꜣt[/t] 'moment' with replacing . In hieratic texts of dyn. XVIII sometimes in personal names without preceding phon. signs for B 3, ex. I͗[t]ꜥḥ[/t]-ms(w) 'Ahmose'. Only very rarely to replace complicated or unusual signs in Dyn. XVIII hieroglyphic, ex. idt 'cow'. Hieratic as substituted for two dets. (see on Z 4) is merely a doubling of .

sign list.description: hieratic substitutes for A 13 or A 14
sign list.notes: Det. death, enemy, exx. m(w)t 'die'; [t]ḫpt[/t] 'decease'; [t]ḫft[/t](y) 'enemy'. In hieroglyphic barely distinguishable from F 20.

sign list.description: hieroglyphic adaption of the hieratic abbreviated form of G 43
sign list.notes:
The hieratic abbreviation of G 43, best transcribed by , occurs with increasing frequency from Dyn. IX onwards. In hieroglyphic w does not become really common until the reign of Akhenaten. Not to be confused with V 1.
For as hieroglyphic adaption of the more cursive hieratic form of G 39, see on H 8. For as hieroglyphic equivalent of the hieratic forms of T 13 and U 39, see U 40.
Det. round, in [t]šnw[/t] 'circuit' and the related words. A different sign from N 18.

Det. break, exx. [t]ḥḏi[/t] 'damage'; gmgm 'break'; divide, exx. wpi 'divide'; [t]psš[/t] 'divide'; [t]ḫbi[/t] 'lessen', 'subtract'; actions involving something crossed or encountered, exx. [t]ḏꜢi[/t] 'cross'; [t]wšb[/t] 'answer'; [t]Ꜣbḫ[/t] 'be united'; also in many words where the reason is not apparent, exx. nkt 'matter', 'trifle'; [t]tꜢš[/t] 'boundary'; wdi 'emit (sound)'. In [t]ḥsb[/t], var. O.K. ḥśb, 'reckon', lit. 'break up (numbers)' (Z 10), the prototype of , has become Aa 2; but in [t]ḥsb[/t] '1/4' the sign has survived as an ideo. Owing to its use as det. in certain stems, has acquired special phon. or semi-phon. values as follows: (1) [t]swꜢ[/t], in [t]swꜢi[/t] (śwꜢi) 'pass by', from [t]swꜢ[/t] ([t]zwꜢ[/t]) 'cut off'; (2) [t]sḏ[/t], in śḏt 'flame', from [t]sḏi[/t] 'break'; (3) [t]ḫbs[/t], in [t]ḫbsw[/t] 'ploughlands'; (4) [t]šbn[/t], in [t]šbn[/t] 'mixed', 'various'; (5) wp, in wp st 'specify it', a phrase serving to introduce details of accounts; (6) wr (reason unknown), exx. sw(r)i 'drink'; [t]ḫpr[/t]-wr, a medicament.
Use as last.

Ideo. (?) in imy 'who is in' and derivatives. Hence (?) phon. imi, ex. imi 'not be'. Since hieratic is often identical with M 42, dyn. XVIII hieroglyphic writes for in wnm 'eat'; so too in [t]wnḏwt[/t] 'subjects'.
Cf. [t]ḫ[/t] 'placenta (?)'. Hence (?) phon. [t]ḫ[/t].

Det. bodily growths or conditions, especially of a morbid kind, exx. wbnw 'wound'; [t]ḫꜢyt[/t] 'disease'; [t]wḫd[/t] 'suffer'; [t]ẖpꜢ[/t] 'navel' (whence phon. [t]ẖp[/t]([t]Ꜣ[/t]) in [t]ḫpw[/t] 'sculptured reliefs'); fat, distended, exx. [t]ḏdꜢ[/t] 'fat'; [t]šfꜢ[/t] 'swell'. Replaces a number of O.K. signs that have become obsolete:--(1) = Pyr V 38, as ideo. or det. in wt 'bandage'; wt 'embalmer'; [t]sdwḫ[/t] 'treat', 'embalm'. (2) = Z 10, as det. in [t]ḥsb[/t] 'reckon'; everywhere else has survived as Z 9. (3) = Pyr F 52 or O.K. N 32, as det. excrement, in [t]ḥs[/t] 'excrement'; smell, in sty 'odor'; clay, in sin 'clay'. (4) = O.K. W 6, as ideo. or det. in [t]wḥꜢt[/t] 'cauldron'; hence phon. [t]wḥꜢ[/t] in [t]WḥꜢt[/t] 'Oasis'. (5) = W 7, as det. in [t]mꜢt[/t] 'granite'; [t]Ꜣbw[/t] 'Elephantine'. (6) = V 32, det. in gw, prob. for [t]gꜢwt[/t] 'bundles'; hence phon. det. [t]gꜢ[/t] in [t]gꜢw[/t] 'be narrow'. (7) = M 41, det. in [t]ꜥš[/t] 'cedar'.

sign list.description: pustule or gland (?) Aa 2 with liquid issuing from it
sign list.notes: Rarer alternative of in its medical or anatomical use, as det. when soft matter or a liquid is meant, exx. [t]wsšt[/t] 'urine'; [t]Ꜣs[/t] 'soft inner parts (?)'. Also det. in [t]sṯ[/t] 'odor'.

sign list.category_group: W, Vessels of stone and earthenware

sign list.description: part of the steering gear of ships ?
sign list.notes: Ideo. or det. in Pyr. [t]ḥpt[/t] in phrase [t]iṯi[/t] [t]ḥpt[/t] 'take the [t]ḥpt[/t]', i.e. 'proceed by boat', r a place; cf. M.K. [t]ḏsr[/t] [t]ḥpwt[/t] 'direct the [t]ḥpwt[/t]' (plur.), i.e. 'sail'. From M.K. there is a word [t]ḥpt[/t] 'oar', but the writing in Pyr. makes it impossible to interpret that word as meaning 'oar' from the start. Hence phon. [t]ḥp[/t], exx. Ḥpy 'Hepy', one of the four sons of Horus; [t]ḥp[/t] 'Apis-bull'. The full stem may have been [t]ḥip[/t], cf. Pyr. [t]ḥip[/t] 'hasten'.
Det. in 𓏏𓌳𓐒 [t]tmꜢ[/t] (from [t]ṯmꜢ[/t]?)[/t] 'mat'. Hence (?) phon. det. [t]ṯmꜢ[/t] in 𓍿𓌳𓐒 var. 𓍿𓌳𓎅𓈅 [t]ṯmꜢ[/t] 'cadaster (?)' or kind of land (?).
Det. or phon. det. sqr (śqr) in 𓋴𓈎𓂋𓐓 [t]varr[/t]. 𓋴𓐓𓌈, 𓐓, 𓋴𓈎𓂋𓌪𓂝 [t]sqr (śqr)[/t] 'smite'.

Ideo. or det. in 𓍑𓏏𓏏𓐖 var. 𓐖𓏏𓏏 [t]ḏꜢtt[/t] 'estate' in the title 𓄓𓏤𓉐𓏤𓈖𓍑𓏏𓏏𓐖 'steward of estate'; the meaning of [t]ḏꜢtt[/t] and the interpretation of 𓐖 [t]here[/t] depends on the not improbable identification of this title with 𓅓𓂋𓉐𓏤𓈖𓈈𓏏𓏤 (var. 𓈙𓏏𓏤) in another tomb of Dyn. XII; the words 𓐖𓏏𓊖 'estate' would in this case read [t]ḏꜢtt[/t]. Hence phon. det. in Dyn. XVIII 𓍑𓍑𓏌𓏏𓐖𓀀𓏥 [t]O[/t].K. 𓍑𓆓𓈒𓏏𓀀𓀀𓀀 [t]ḏꜢḏꜢt[/t] 'magistrates', 'assesors'. For an unknown reason, phon. qn, exx. 𓐖𓈖𓏛 [t]qn[/t] 'complete', 'be complete'; 𓐖𓈖𓎅 [t]qn[/t] 'mat'. In hieratic 𓐖 [t]sometimes[/t] stands not only for itself but also for certain other signs, whence confusion have resulted both in modern transcriptions and in actual hieroglyphic texts. Thus 𓐖 is found for (1) 𓈈 [t]N[/t] 24 in hierogl. 𓐖𓏏𓏤 [t]spꜢt[/t] 'district'; (2) for 𓎙 [t]V[/t] 26 in hieratic 𓐖𓆓𓈇𓏤 var. 𓐖𓈇 [t]ꜥḏ[/t] 'desert edge'. Possibly with some confusion with 𓊃 [t]O[/t] 34, 𓐖𓏏𓈉 is found used in Dyn. XVIII hieroglyphic for smt 'desert', 'necropolis', as a mediating var. 𓋴𓏏𓅓𓐖𓏏𓈅𓏤𓈉 [t]proves[/t]; for this reason the name of the Dyn. I king 𓍷𓐖𓏏𓏭 [t]vꜥr[/t]. 𓍷𓐖𓏏𓏭𓈉 is possibly to be read Zmty rather than ḪꜢsty.
Det. in 𓐍𓅱𓂧𓐗 [t]ḫwd[/t] 'rich'.
Det. in 𓂧𓂋𓆑𓐘𓏛 [t]drf[/t] 'writing'.

For an unkown reason, phon. [t]mꜢꜥ[/t] in 𓌳𓐙𓂝𓏏𓆄 var. 𓐙𓏏𓏛 [t]mꜢꜥt[/t] 'truth' and the related words. Note specifically often the writing with 𓐙𓊤 [t]mꜢꜥ-ḫrw[/t] 'true of voice'. As a pedastal det. in 𓍿𓈖𓏏𓏏𓐙 [t]ṯntt[/t] 'raised platform', a unique writing (?).
For 𓌶, 𓌷, see U 4, U 5.
Use as last.

sign list.description: hardly the two ribs of an oryx as has been suggested
sign list.notes: Ideo. or det. in O.K. 𓇋𓅓𓐛 [t]im[/t], plur. 𓐛𓐛𓐛 [t]imw[/t], a part of the body. Hence (?) phon. im, exx. 𓇋𓅓𓐛𓂟 [t]imi[/t] 'give', imper.; 𓇋𓐛𓅓𓅱𓊛 [t]imw[/t] 'boat'; also, from Dyn. XVIII on, phon. m. Ideo. also in 𓐛 var. 𓐞 [t]gs[/t], var. Pyr. 𓎼𓋴𓐜, 𓐜𓏤 [t]g[/t]ś 'side', 'half'. Hence phon. gs, exx. 𓐛𓊃𓏊𓀜 var. 𓎼𓊃𓂝 [t]gs[/t] 'anoint'; 𓐛𓏤𓍘𓇋𓆱 [t]gsti[/t] 'palette'.
Use as last.

sign list.description: alternative form of 𓐛 Aa 13 (Dyn. XVIII)
sign list.notes: Use as last.
Used only in 𓐞 var. 𓐞𓏤 [t]gs[/t] 'side', 'half' and as phon. gs.

sign list.description: back of something (O.K. and M.K. form)
sign list.notes: Ideo. in 𓐟 [t]sꜢ[/t] (śꜢ)[/t] 'back', Copitc soi. Hence phon. [t]sꜢ[/t] (śꜢ), exx. 𓋴𓐟𓄿𓅱𓏏𓊅𓊅𓊅 [t]sꜢwt[/t] 'walls'; 𓋴𓐟𓄿𓀁 [t]sꜢi[/t] 'be satiated'; 𓈙𓋴𓐟𓄿𓄃𓏛 [t]šsꜢ[/t] 'be skilled'.
Use as last. In group-writing 𓐠 [t]or[/t] 𓐠𓏤 is used for s.
For unkown reason, phon. det. [t]ḥr[/t], exx. 𓁷𓂋𓐡𓂡 [t]ḥr[/t] 'prepare'; 𓁷𓂋𓇋𓇋𓏏𓐡𓂡𓏥 [t]ḥryt[/t] 'dread'. Also det. in 𓅷𓄿𓂋𓐡𓂡 [t]ṯꜢr[/t] 'preserve (?)' and derivatives.
For unknown reason, phon. [t]ꜥpr[/t] in 𓐢𓂋𓏛 var. 𓂝𓊪𓂋𓐢 [t]ꜥpr[/t] 'equip' and derivatives.
Ideo. (?) or det. in 𓐣𓂝𓏛 [t]varr[/t]. 𓐤, 𓅱𓆓𓂝𓐣 [t]O[/t].K. 𓅱𓆓𓐣 [t]wḏꜥ[/t] 'sever', 'judge'. In M.K. coffins 𓐣 [t]or[/t] 𓐣𓀭 is sometimes used as a substitute for the god 𓃩 [t]Stẖ[/t] 'Seth'.

sign list.description: combination of 𓐣 Aa 21 and 𓂝 D 36
sign list.notes: Use as last.
Ideo. (?) in 𓐧𓀀 var. 𓄥𓄿 [t]smꜢ[/t], var. O.K. 𓋴𓐧 ś([t]mꜢ[/t]), title of a priest whose function consisted in clothing the god (Min, Horus, etc.).
Phon. det. sbi (śbi) in 𓋴𓃀𓇋𓐨𓀏 [t]sbi (śbi)[/t] 'rebel'. Often replaced by 𓌙 [t]T[/t] 14.

For an unknown reason, phon. [t]nḏ[/t], exx. 𓐩𓏌𓀁 [t]varr[/t]. 𓈖𓆓𓐩𓏌𓀁, 𓐩𓆓𓏌 [t]nḏ[/t] 'ask', 'inquire'; 𓐩𓏌𓐩𓏌 var. 𓈖𓆓𓈖𓆓𓐩𓏌𓀁 [t]nḏnḏ[/t] 'take counsel'. Except in 𓇋𓐩𓆓𓏛𓁷𓏤 [t]inḏ[/t] [t]ḥr[/t] 'hail to' 𓐩 is usually accompanied in M.E. by 𓏌 [t]W[/t] 24.

sign list.description: an instrument used by bricklayers ? (different from M 40 and P 11)
sign list.notes: Ideo. (?) in 𓐪𓂧𓏌𓀨 var. 𓈎𓂧𓐪𓀨 [t]qd[/t] 'build', 'fashion (pots)' and related words.
Use as last.

sign list.description: ornamental chevaux de frise on top of walls, cf. O 11 (sometimes written horizontally)
sign list.notes: Ideo. or det. in 𓌨𓎡𓂋𓐬 [t]ẖkr[/t] 'be adorned'; 𓐬𓅱𓏛𓈒𓈒𓈒 [t]ẖkrw[/t] 'ornament', 'adornment' and the related words.
Use as last.
